title: Unprompted coordination through shared memory in LLM agents: a locked two-implementation replication and extension
abstract: arXiv:2611.12412v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Coordination between large language-model agents has become a central question for AI safety and software engineering, as such agents are deployed in groups that share infrastructure. Existing research typically tells the agents that partners exist or asks them to coordinate. Whether coordination arises through shared state alone, with nothing disclosing that anyone else is present, is the key question for deployments that share caches and memory between agents, yet it has rarely been examined, and to our knowledge not with independent replication; this study does both. Four agents each received a short arithmetic task and a key-value store presented to each as its own scratch space; two held complementary halves of one computation, and no prompt mentioned other agents, sharing or collaboration. For reliability, the environment was rebuilt independently from a written protocol, and both implementations ran under hashed locks on

translated_title: LLM智能体通过共享内存实现的无提示协调：一项加锁双重实现的复现与扩展研究
translated_abstract: 大型语言模型智能体之间的协调已成为AI安全与软件工程的核心问题，因为这类智能体通常以共享基础设施的群体形式部署。现有研究通常会告知智能体伙伴的存在，或直接要求它们进行协调。而仅通过共享状态——在没有任何信息透露其他参与者存在的情况下——协调是否会自发产生，这对于在智能体之间共享缓存与内存的部署场景而言是一个关键问题，但该问题鲜有研究，据我们所知也从未经过独立复现；本研究两者兼顾。四个智能体各自收到一个简短的算术任务和一个键值存储，每个智能体都将该存储视为自己的暂存空间；其中两个智能体持有同一计算中互补的两半，且所有提示均未提及智能体、共享或协作。为保证可靠性，实验环境依据书面协议独立重建，两种实现均在哈希锁机制下运行。
tldr: 本研究通过双重独立实现的复现与扩展首次证实：即使提示中完全没有提及其他智能体、共享或协作的存在，LLM智能体也能仅凭共享内存状态自发产生协调行为。
en_tdlr: This study independently replicates and extends the finding that LLM agents can spontaneously coordinate through shared memory alone, even when no prompt discloses the existence of other agents, sharing, or collaboration.
